 By WRAL Staff
 North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson has joined a federal lawsuit against Dollar General, accusing the bargain chain of illegally overcharging customers.
 During a news conference on Tuesday, Jackson said the company routinely charged consumers more at the register than the prices displayed on shelves, price tags and advertisements.
 Other WRAL Top Stories
 “We’re suing Dollar General because they’re ripping people off, and they know it," Jackson said. "They’ve failed state inspections and been told over and over to fix these mistakes. They haven’t, so we’ll see them in court."
 19 other states, along with the Federal Trade Commission, are listed as plaintiffs in the 95-page lawsuit, which said Dollar General engaged in deceptive pricing practices, costing consumers millions and "failed to correct the issue despite extensive corporate knowledge of the problem."
 North Carolina has over 1,000 Dollar General locations, with at least one in nearly every town, according to the NC Department of Justice. Jackson said inspectors found 400 pricing inaccuracies at 10 North Carolina Dollar General locations in 28 inspections over a two-year period. 
 Last week, the North Carolina Department of Agriculture fined 10 Dollar General locations in eight NC counties, accusing them of overcharging customers. Nine other stores from different companies were also fined for price-scanning errors, according to the department. 
 "Over a million North Carolinians shop at Dollar General every week, and they are ripping people off," Jackson said.
 In a statement, Dollar General said the company "has enhanced our price-accuracy processes and remains committed to continuous improvement."
 "The lawsuit filed today by the Federal Trade Commission and several States suggests that we have abandoned our mission and willfully disregarded the affordability needs of our customers. Nothing could be further from the truth," Dollar General wrote. 
 The company wrote that it first learned of the FTC’s investigation in early February, and that it has cooperated with regulators. Dollar General was "surprised" that the federal regulatory agency and 20 states filed the lawsuit instead of responding to the company's counteroffer of an initial FTC monetary demand, according to an online company statement.
 The lawsuit seeks a stop to the alleged pricing practices, civil penalties, and money back for impacted customers. 
 What shoppers can do:
 Check receipts before leaving the store 
 Ask store to correct the price if charged more 
 File complaint with N.C. Department of Agriculture Consumer Services' Standards Division by filling out the online complaint form or call 984-236-4751.
 The FTC and states allege these practices violate the FTC Act, the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and state consumer protection laws.
